messages.author: da31ad9cadc1d9b2
messages.subject: Afffy 6.0 using Nsp I only
parts:
Dear List:

One of my collaborators wants to do the arrays using NspI only. It
seems like a reasonable idea since only a small fraction of the
probesets are queried by StyI alone. Can aroma.affymetrix be used to
analyze such arrays or does it implicitly use that the fragments come
from a mixture of StyI and NspI processed DNA? Also can the probesets
queried by StyI alone be removed from the precessing (from
normalization down all the steps that follow).

Thanks,
Venkat

messages.author: 8ae1efaa2cf53fab
messages.subject: Re: Afffy 6.0 using Nsp I only
parts:
Hi Venkat,

As far as I am aware, when you buy 6.0 arrays, you get both Nsp and
Sty arrays (http://www.affymetrix.com/products/arrays/specific/
genome_wide_snp6/genome_wide_snp_6.affx), so it would seem odd to
choose not to use a particular array (that you have already
purchased). This is different from the *500K* arrays where you can
specifically purchase arrays just for Nsp *or* Sty (http://
www.affymetrix.com/products/arrays/specific/500k.affx). If your
collaborator chooses to use the 500K arrays, and chooses to use just
Nsp, then that is fine, aroma.affymetrix can analyse arrays from just
a particular enzyme. See this page:
http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/total-copy-number-analysis?hl=en
for details.

cheers

Lavinia.

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: Afffy 6.0 using Nsp I only
parts:
Hi,

yes by only hybridizing NspI targets you "only" miss about 160,000
SNPs on GWS6, since all CN probes are designed for NspI and several of
the SNPs designed for StyI are by chance also on the NspI fragments as
well. So, it makes sense to try this idea out. I guess except from
the obvious of saving some money on not purchasing the StyI kit, the
main advantage is probably that you save a few hours (days?) of work
in each batch.

You will be able to process the data "as is" through the
aroma.affymetrix pipeline. You can even use the same annotation files
etc. Of course, the question is what the result will be. The
crosstalk calibration should be fine and so the summarization. The
fragment-length normalization will treat the data as if you hybridized
StyI target as well - the StyI-only signals should be close to zero
(whatever that is) and the model will be fitted to this. I cannot see
why the current model shouldn't still work, but I might have overseen
something.

One could also consider extending the model where one filter out
certain probes (here StyI probes). Filtering of probes have been
requested before and it is on the todo list (not very high up though).
Then, with some modifications to the fragment-length
model/algorithm/implementation, an NspI-only GWS5/6 data set would
effectively be processed as if it was a (more dense) Mapping250K_Nsp
chip.

I'd say, if you already have the data, give the current setup a try
and see if you get decent results. Any modifications will only get
better from there. One warning though: If you one day decide to
hybridize with both enzymes, I doubt that you can easily mix the CEL
files from NspI-only and NspI+StyI hybs. The reference signals
(theta_R) will probably not be comparible, especially not for the
probes target by both enzymes.

I would be interested in looking at this kind of data for another
reason - I'm comparing the different generations of Affymetrix chips
and this data could bring some more understanding to the overall
picture.

Cheers

Henrik

with a mix of NspI-only and NspI+StyI hybs is more
statistical/biological rather than computational/practical. Maybe I
misunderstood you or vice versa.

I assume that this CDF is an identical copy of the corresponding
GenomeWideSNP_6 CDF, correct?

I just want to make you aware that you're entering a bit mined areas
here, because you rely on the fact that the chip type of an Affymetrix
CDF is inferred from the filename and not an internal file header.
This is actually the case, but one day Affymetrix might put out a new
CDF file format where there file header is used. But, alright for now

>
> The ufl (and ugp) still have a a chip type of GenomeWideSNP_6 instead of the
> new one. Will this warning cause a problem? Can the footer be changed to
> the "right" platform?

I guess this illustrate my point raised above.

Yes, you can update the footer using readFooter(), update the list
structure, and use writeFooter() to write it back.

I'm not sure I understand where you are heading. Is your next step to
update the UFL file such that all StyI length are NAs? If so, it may
or may not work out of the box, but lets see; if not, it is a good
test for now.

I think an slightly different and better approach of what you doing is
to stick with chip type name 'GenomeWideSNP_6' and append the
additional tag 'NspI-only' in addition to the existing 'Full' tag.
This way you would keep all your annotation files for the identical
chip type under the same path, i.e.
annotationData/chipTypes/GenomeWideSNP_6/. Note that I try to stick
to the definition of a chip type as something that never changes after
the chip is produced in the factory - the probes will always be the
same for GWS6 - it is only the annotation that gets updated. This is
along the lines what others did with the exon array - there are a few
custom made CDF, but the all live in the same chip type directory.
This way you will also be able to reuse the existing CDF (and UGP).
So, if you are only creating a custom UFL, then do name it as:

annotationData/chipTypes/GenomeWideSNP_6/
GenomeWideSNP_6,Full,na24,HB20080214,VS20081009,NspI-only.ufl

or similar. You can update the footer with comments of what you've done.

Does this make more sense?

However, I'd say, if you already have the data, make sure to give the
existing pipeline a try and treat it as there are StyI fragments as
well. *I think* that CRMA will treat it only as weak signals, but it
won't introduce bias (just a bit of noise).

Cheers

/Henrik

> only with those from NspI+StyI hybs. I believe I misunderstood your
> comment that the reference signals not being comparable. My mistake
> is probably believing that analyzing the two kinds of CEL files using
> the same annotation data can cause problems. Will I be OK as long as
> I keep them in separate rawData branches?

Yes, keeping them as separate data sets will lower the risk for mixing
them up. It is easier to process them independently of each other and
if decide you want to give it a try to process them together, you can
always merge them in the code. For instance, by doing:

csR <- AffymetrixCelSet$byName("foo", cdf=cdf);
csR2 <- AffymetrixCelSet$byName("bar", cdf=cdf);
append(csR, csR2);
rm(csR2);

the 'csR' object will contain the foo files with the bar files
appended at the end. The (output) name of what you process with csR
will be decided by the first file in the csR set (this is always the
case for any data set). By adding a tag in the first processing step
you can separate the merged data sets from the non-merge one, e.g.

qn <- QuantileNormalization(csR, tags="bar,*")

/Henrik

> at a future point.
